newsitem.title: USA: US budget deal ends threat of delayed CRP entry.
newsitem.headline: US budget deal ends threat of delayed CRP entry.

text.p: The fiscal 1998 budget plan pending in Congress ends the threat of a one-year delay in accepting some land into the Conservation Reserve, lawmakers and a White House official said Tuesday.

The deferral had been proposed as a way to offset the $65 million cost of stopping development of the New World mine near Yellowstone National Park. Due to opposition, the funds now would come from a land and water conservation fund.
Kathleen McGinty, chair of the Council on Environmental Quality, and Barbara Cubin, who chairs a House Resources subcommittee, described the new plan during a hearing.

Budget negotiators, who completed work last week, reserved $700 million in fiscal 1998 budget authority for "priority federal land acquisitions and exchanges," McGinty said. The administration's top priorities are $65 million to "buy out" the New World mine and $250 million to acquire the Headwaters forest in California, she said.
New World was a project of Crown Butte Mines Inc.
Crown Butte chairman Karl Elers said the buy-out plan "provided a practical resolution to a unique set of circumstances" and was in its best interests.
Environmentalists have supported the buyout. They have said the mine, among other problems, posed the threat of water pollution just upstream from Yellowstone National Park.
